sections.h2: Where a Scott County bill comes from
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The PVA fixes what a parcel is worth. The sheriff mails the bill and takes payment, and never sets a value. The sheriff collects for 28 districts, among them the state, the county, school systems, fire and library districts and, by contract, some cities. Mailing normally happens on November 1. Dispute a value? Call the PVA at (502) 863-7885. Have a payment question? Call the sheriff at (502) 863-7855.

Because the sheriff bills for so many districts at once, one statement can look larger than the county rate you expect. Ask the office for a line-by-line breakdown if you want to see how much goes to schools, fire protection and the library.

Georgetown adds its own levy. City hall's Clerk's Office takes payment over the counter, by post or by phone, and lookup and online payment run through the city's OpenGov portal. Bills from before 2025 are found through the city's Tax Master service. A house inside Georgetown carries a city bill in addition to the county one.

sections.h2: Scott County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Scott County lies north of Lexington and is counted in the Lexington-Fayette metro. Georgetown is the county seat and the largest city, with Sadieville and Stamping Ground as the smaller ones. The county grew from 47,173 residents in 2010 to 57,155 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 62,262, up 8.9 percent since 2020. Lexington is roughly 16 miles south by way of I-75, and Cincinnati about 69 miles north.

Prices sit well above the Kentucky norm. A typical owner-occupied home is $288,500 and typical household income is $85,158. The county has 22,642 households and an estimated 25,010 housing units. Owners hold 71.7 percent of occupied units, and middle rent is $1,247. Owner costs run $1,637 a month with a mortgage and $514 without one. Builders took out 393 permits in 2025, so a resale competes with new construction.

Toyota's Georgetown plant anchors the local job base. One district, Scott County Schools, serves the whole county, so families relocating here will ask which zone your address falls in. Look it up before you list.

KRS 134.015 sets the calendar, and the sheriff follows it.

  • By November 1: a 2 percent discount for paying in full.
  • Through December 31: the face amount.
  • January: 5 percent added.
  • Later payment: 10 percent added.

Whoever held title on January 1 owes that year's tax personally, and a delinquent bill leaves a lien on the land itself. Spell out the split in your sales contract so the closing agent knows what to deduct from your proceeds. A spring closing usually means the buyer's side pays the bill that arrives the next November, and the seller credits their share of the months already passed.

sections.h2: What happens when a bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
Around April 15 the sheriff's unpaid bills move to the County Clerk. The county attorney writes in May, offering payment agreements to eligible owners, and again in June. Every year the sequence is the same, with only the dates shifting.

Scott County Clerk delinquent tax calendar
WhenStep
April 15Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk
May and JuneCounty Attorney mails notices and offers payment agreements
June 30Deadline to sign a payment agreement
July 1Advertising costs attach to remaining bills
Late AugustLast chance to pay, then the sale in the third-floor Fiscal Court Room

The clerk takes cash, cashier's checks, money orders and cards, and a 2.75 percent vendor fee applies to cards. For payoff figures call the clerk at (502) 863-7875, extension 2260, or the County Attorney at (502) 863-7870 about agreements.

• Sheriff (current-year bills): 240 Caleb Conley Way and 120 N Hamilton St, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Clerk (delinquent bills, deeds, motor vehicles): 101 E Main Street, Georgetown, weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • County Attorney: 198 E Washington St, Georgetown.
  • Georgetown-Scott County Revenue Commission (occupational and business tax): (502) 603-5860.

Property and vehicle taxes are not collected at the county Treasurer's office.

sections.h2: How to contest a valuation or claim an exemption
sections.html:
A conference with the PVA comes first. Only after it can you petition the local appeals board, which wants comparable sales, repair bids or similar proof. An appeal does not suspend the bill, so pay on the value you claim while it runs. Gather your evidence before the meeting, and keep copies of everything you hand over.

Owners past 65 and those totally disabled can claim the homestead exemption through the PVA. The state's deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and the PVA can confirm the figure for the current year.

If your house sits inside Georgetown, you have two bills to track. The county bill comes from the sheriff. The city bill comes from city hall, where the Clerk's Office takes payment over the counter, by post or by phone.

For a current-year city bill, use the OpenGov portal for lookup and online payment. For years before 2025, the city's Tax Master service is the place to search. Print both receipts before closing day, because a buyer's title agent will want proof that neither bill is open. A house outside the city limits has no city bill, which is worth telling buyers who are comparing addresses.

A delinquent bill will show up in the title search, so deal with it early.

  • Ask the County Clerk for a payoff, since it holds delinquent bills after April 15.
  • If the County Attorney offers a payment agreement, you must sign by June 30.
  • Give the closing agent the final figure so it comes out of your proceeds.
  • If you own a house inside Georgetown, check the city bill too, since it is paid separately.

Bring a few things when you visit an office: a photo ID, your deed or closing paperwork, and the bill itself or the parcel address. Staff can pull up the account faster with the address, and written payoff numbers are what the closing agent will ask for. If you share ownership with a spouse or heir, have the other owner's name ready too, since payment and records are tied to the owner of record.

A direct cash sale works well when back taxes and repairs are both stacked up, because the buyer does not wait on a lender and the tax is paid from the sale money.

faqs.q: Which office takes Scott County property tax payments?
faqs.a: For the current year, the Scott County Sheriff's Office at (502) 863-7855. Around April 15 unpaid bills go to the County Clerk, and Georgetown's own city bill is paid through the city.

faqs.q: When is the Scott County tax sale?
faqs.a: In late August each year, in the third-floor Fiscal Court Room. Pay before the day of the sale to keep a bill out of it, and ask the clerk at (502) 863-7875 for the current date.

faqs.q: Is there a payment plan for delinquent Scott County tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. The County Attorney mails a May notice describing agreements for eligible owners, and June 30 is the cutoff to sign one. The office answers at (502) 863-7870.

faqs.q: Does turning 65 give a Scott County owner the homestead exemption automatically?
faqs.a: No. File at the PVA, (502) 863-7885, with proof of age. The state deduction for 2025 and 2026 was $49,100.

faqs.q: Does Georgetown bill property tax separately from the county?
faqs.a: Yes, the city bills its own property tax. You can search and pay through the city's OpenGov portal or at the City Clerk's Office.
